items.summary: Anthropic launched OSS Scanner, a free opt-in tool that audits enrolled open-source projects with its strongest models including Claude Mythos. Reports go directly to maintainers without human review; after the first 11 days it recorded 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings. Of 97 audited critical and high findings, 85 (88%) met Anthropic's disclosure bar, with only one false positive. wolfSSL independently confirmed most reports valid.
items.title: Anthropic Launches Free AI Vulnerability Scanner for Critical Open-Source Projects

items.summary: Dora Hoan, global CEO and co-founder of Best World International, has been elected chair of the World Federation of Direct Selling Associations (WFDSA), becoming the first Asia-Pacific leader to hold the role in its 48-year history. During her term she plans to strengthen engagement with regulators, raise ethics and consumer-protection standards, promote responsible AI adoption, support women’s entrepreneurship, and improve communication among member associations and companies. Her priorities were outlined at WFDSA’s 18th world congress in Incheon, South Korea (Oct 19–21), where she noted that 69% of Best World Lifestyle’s distributors are women aged 44 and below.
items.title: Best World CEO Dora Hoan Elected WFDSA Chair

items.summary: Melissa Low, a Telok Blangah resident, wrote in response to discussions about Maju Forest and Gillman Forest. She welcomed the Government's engagement with nature groups but asked that residents be invited to review materially revised planning options before they are settled. Residents presented the Better Plan on Sept 1, seeking housing needs while retaining the forest.
items.title: Maju and Gillman residents seek input before revised forest plans are finalised

items.summary: Ramesh Balan wrote a forum post arguing that Singaporeans should accept wild birds rather than fear them. He acknowledged genuine discomfort around large birds but framed the issue as part of broader planning to bring nature into heartland areas and preserve biodiversity. The author noted chickens and roosters reflect kampung heritage, cited wildlife adapting to urban spaces, and pointed to the City in Nature vision. He called for balance between human comfort, safety, conservation, and coexistence.
items.title: Singaporean urges coexistence with urban wildlife, including fowl

items.summary: A roundup of notable AI-powered wearables aims to bring artificial intelligence into daily life through productivity tools and companion devices. The list includes pendants, rings, wristbands, and portable gadgets from companies such as Bee — now owned by Amazon after its July 2025 acquisition — Friend, Limitless (formerly Rewind), Muse Charm, Nirva, Omi, Plaud’s NotePin, Rabbit R1, and Sandbar. Devices range in price from $49.99 to $299 and offer features like transcription, summaries, reminders, mood recognition, and voice interaction. Friend has drawn criticism over its subway ad campaign in NYC, where people vandalized the ads with messages such as “surveillance capitalism.” Several products remain unreleased or upcoming, including Meta’s Muse Charm and Sandbar’s Stream ring.
items.title: Hottest AI Wearables and Gadgets on the Market

items.summary: The Western Australian government says it is “extremely disappointed” and seeks an expedited cost recovery from the consultancy firm Deloitte after errors were found in a feasibility study on merging the University of Western Australia, Curtin university and Murdoch university. The report paid for at $166,000 contained AI-hallucinated references and hundreds of millions of dollars in cost discrepancies: under its high-cost scenario it showed totals that diverged by $260m from reported figures; a low-cost scenario showed a $311m gap. Governance experts said the errors discredit the report and called for rework, while Deloitte acknowledged using generative AI to support research collation but had earlier dismissed the mistakes as minor. The WA government says any errors will be corrected in a review that will re-issue the report; Murdoch’s vice-chancellor Prof Andrew Deeks rejected the merger outright. Deloitte did not respond to questions from Guardian Australia.
items.title: WA Government Demands Cost Recovery from Deloitte Over Flawed University Merger Report

items.summary: The Australian soap opera Neighbours is being recut with an AI-assisted tool called RedSnapper into a vertical microdrama for phones, initially focusing on Margot Robbie’s character Donna Freedman and producing about 150 minutes of content. RoseBerry Media repurposed original episodes through its Epis platform using the technology. Cast members Stefan Dennis and Matthew Werkmeister voiced concerns over consent and compensation, with Werkmeister calling it a “money grab for Fremantle”. Fremantle defended the project as reusing only previously broadcast footage, while RedSnapper’s spokesperson said it does not generate new scenes or alter likenesses. The move arrives amid an estimated $15bn vertical serials market, prompting calls from union leader Adam Portellin and Werkmeister for stronger AI regulation.
items.title: Neighbours AI microdrama draws cast criticism

items.summary: Researchers from Stanford and UC Berkeley released TokenGate, a module that adds learned token pruning to pretrained large language models. The team reports time-to-first-token speeds of 1.4x to 11.3x with no accuracy loss, peak prefill memory reductions of 1.5x to 3.4x, and performance tested on contexts up to 128k tokens. Token-gated attention makes top-K selection trainable using a mixture-of-experts router approach. Code and checkpoints are available on GitHub under Apache-2.0.
items.title: Stanford and UC Berkeley researchers introduce TokenGate for faster long-context prefill

items.summary: A Climate Central analysis shared with The Trace estimates that climate change made high temperatures more likely, contributing to roughly 2,000 shootings between 2021 and 2025 across the 100 most violent U.S. cities. Kristina Dahl of Climate Central stated that in aggregate, climate change is raising gun violence risk nationwide. The study modeled hypothetical cooler temperatures using 22 climate models plus real records, finding Philadelphia's typical day was about 2.4 degrees Fahrenheit hotter due to climate change, linked to an estimated 149 additional shootings over five years. No individual shooting was attributed to heat; researchers examined aggregate city-level relationships instead. Experts caution that temperature is one of many factors and note historical misuse linking race and weather. The burden likely falls on disadvantaged neighborhoods with less green space and cooling access.
items.title: Climate Change's Rising Toll on Gun Violence in U.S. Cities

items.summary: The US military has granted Elon Musk's SpaceX access to restricted space tracking data, prompting concerns about national security and whether the Trump administration is handing over orbit traffic control to a political donor. The move follows Doge firing staff from Traccs in 2025 and repeated attempts to defund it. Industry observers warn of monopoly risks and a 'vendor lock' scenario. Cole Donovan called SpaceX the de facto source for coordination, likening the deal to giving a trucking company control of traffic lights. The Space Force said it exchanges commercial data sources for access to controlled information benefiting the government. A former Noaa official praised Starlink's responsiveness while criticizing the lack of governance framework. Craig Holman of Public Citizen framed the access as rewarding a donor with lucrative contracts.
items.title: US Military Grants SpaceX Access to Sensitive Space Tracking Data

items.summary: Audi announced a $4bn (£3bn) investment in its first US plant, near Macon, Georgia, to build the Q7, Q8 and Q9 SUVs. Chief executive Gernot Döllner unveiled it at a Donald Trump rally on Saturday night. The factory will produce 200,000 vehicles annually and create 4,500 jobs. Audi faces EU import tariffs of up to 15%, while its parent Volkswagen reports tariff costs reaching €5bn (£4.2bn) yearly.
items.title: Audi opens $4bn US factory amid job cuts

items.summary: Adani Airport Holdings Limited reworked its plan to relocate international flight operations from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA), scaling the target down to 33% and starting with Indian carriers while foreign airlines keep opposing the move. On Sunday, IndiGo and Air India announced a phased shift of their international services—mainly West Asia routes—to NMIA beginning in early 2027.
items.title: Adani scales back Mumbai air shift as IndiGo, Air India begin phased move

items.summary: The Gulf News reported that four Indian passport service centres across the UAE have closed permanently. Alhind, which provides outsourced services for the Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Consulate in Dubai, issued an advisory directing applicants to two remaining open centres.
items.title: Four Indian Passport Centres in UAE Close Permanently, Applicants Redirected

items.summary: NPR reports that Netflix is laying off about 6% of its workforce, following the release of this week's quarterly earnings. The company describes itself as regrouping while revenue growth has slowed and it works to overhaul its programming unit. NPR notes it does not offer or accept money for coverage.
items.title: Netflix Cuts Workforce as Revenue Growth Slows After Earnings Release

items.summary: As Chancellor John Healey finalises his first Budget, BBC reporters examine how the 'squeezed middle' are coping with rising costs. Interviewee Dawn Fazackerley-King says there is 'no more fat to trim,' warning her mortgage rate could rise from 1. 4% to about 5. 3%, adding roughly £250 a month. Another interviewee, Jessica Taylor on Universal Credit, describes living 'month to month.' An Office for National Statistics survey found that in August 55% of adults said their cost of living had increased compared with the previous month, lower than 62% in August 2025 and 79% in April. The BBC contacted HM Treasury for comment. Healey has pledged not to raise income tax, National Insurance or VAT while following Labour's fiscal rules; Prime Minister Andy Burnham promised 'breathing space' through a £2 bus fare cap and lower electricity VAT. The Office for Budget Responsibility forecasts real household disposable income rising about 0.
items.title: Chancellor Healey's Budget Offers No Relief for Squeezed Middle

items.summary: BBC Verify examines how Chancellor John Healey might raise money without increasing income tax, VAT or National Insurance, which Labour's 2024 manifesto pledged not to do. Taxing banks more is widely expected but may deter investment; raising taxes on gambling machines from 20% to 40% could yield £275m-£460m a year; making online marketplaces collect VAT might add around £1bn, though Amazon estimates only £700m. Together these measures would raise at most about £3.5bn annually - small against the sums needed for welfare cuts and defence spending, which remain politically contested.
items.title: Four tax and spending options Labour could use in the Budget

items.summary: On the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, CGTN's Xu Qinduo visited a special exhibition in Beijing. The route from Jiangxi to northern Shaanxi is described as moving from strategic retreat to turning point and hardship to legend. The history is presented as transcending borders because it symbolizes human courage under extreme conditions.
items.title: CGTN Reporter Visits Long March Exhibition on Anniversary

items.summary: A commentator frames an expected wave of roughly 100,000 US students visiting China over the next five years as transformative. He traces it to President Xi Jinping's late-September call for such visits and notes that a similar earlier target was exceeded in about two and a half years. Drawing on his own trips abroad and cited academic research, he argues direct experience reshapes how young Americans see the world. A student quoted from 2025 described Chinese people as 'inviting and friendly,' while another compared lives as both different and alike.
items.title: Xi's invitation may draw a century of US students to China

items.summary: Artificial intelligence is changing how Hollywood makes movies, enabling filmmakers to create entire scenes with smaller crews and a fraction of traditional production budgets. As the technology advances, concerns are growing over the future of actors, production studios and thousands of jobs.
items.title: AI Threatens Traditional Hollywood Filmmaking as Concerns Grow Over Jobs and Studios

items.summary: France's National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor's Office (PNAT) announced on Sunday that the suspected gunman in Friday's Trappes shooting has had his police custody suspended for psychiatric reasons and transferred to a Paris police prefecture observation unit. The 26-year-old suspect killed one person, identified as MMA fighter Pengo Bossio Wangi, and injured five others including a critically wounded child.
items.title: Trappes shooting suspect moved to psychiatric unit after custody suspended

items.summary: Ahead of a UK-EU summit in Brussels next month, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he supports an 'honest discussion' about re-adapting free movement between the UK and the EU. In a Sunday Times interview, he ruled out ever joining the Schengen zone or adopting the Euro. Nigel Farage called his comments a betrayal of Brexit Britain.
items.title: Burnham favours honest discussion on EU free movement return

items.summary: A Royal Australian College of General Practitioners report finds the proportion of Australians bulk-billed for all GP care rose to 63%, up from 56% in both 2024 and 2025, following government incentives. Australia Institute health economist Luke Slawomirski cautioned that the survey covers about 7% of GPs and urged judgment by patient outcomes rather than bulk-billing rates alone.
items.title: RACGP Report Shows Surge in Bulk-Billed GP Care Amid Concerns Over Access

items.summary: Uganda reports no confirmed active Ebola cases, yet it has drawn scrutiny after both Kenya's first patient and a Nigerian woman are linked to travel through Entebbe International Airport on October 3. African health officials say the patients may have crossed paths there, though transmission is unconfirmed. Switzerland disputes Uganda's account that the Nigerian patient visited DR Congo, saying she never traveled there; WHO and Africa CDC have not confirmed her DRC visit either. Kenya continues searching for an unidentified contact of its deceased patient. Authorities in Abuja intensify tracing amid renewed anxiety over outbreaks.
items.title: Uganda Cites No Active Ebola Cases Amid Cross-Border Investigation

items.summary: Lucas Pinheiro Braathen won the opening men's giant slalom of the 2025-26 Alpine ski season in Sölden, Austria. The Norwegian-born Brazilian was 0.24 seconds faster than his nearest rival on a first run down Rettenbach glacier piste that strong winds had shortened. He beat Switzerland's Loic Meillard by 0.48 and finished ahead of Marco Odermatt, who went fastest on the second run but placed third at 0.01 slower. Braathen said opening in this way felt like a relief after his Olympic success.
items.title: Brazil's Pinheiro Braathen Opens Alpine Season with Giant Slalom Win

items.summary: In the People's Action Party's first leadership ballot since its May 2025 electoral mandate, only one new name appeared among the top 12 choices. Institute of Policy Studies Senior Research Fellow Gillian Koh attributes this cautious renewal to a broader regional and global 'polycrisis,' noting that younger office holders will need more time and exposure to win over party cadres. The vote favored experienced fourth-generation leaders for continuity, with former Secretary-General Lee Hsien Loong and K Shanmugam retained. Acting Minister Zaqy Mohamad and Tan See Leng were co-opted after ranking among the 14 highest voters. Koh emphasizes that more work is needed to build party faith in younger ministers.
items.title: PAP Cadres Favor Experienced Leadership in Renewal Vote

items.summary: French officials reported more than 1,300 arrests after hundreds of thousands joined Saturday’s mostly peaceful protests nationwide. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez warned the figure would rise as counting continued. Demonstrations turned violent in some cities at nightfall, though police avoided last weekend’s rioting. Nunez estimated turnout at 410,00 while the CGT union claimed nearly double that amount.
items.title: France Arrests Over 1,300 Amid Widespread Protests

items.summary: FRANCE 24 looks back at striking images from the past week, covering student protests across France over the weekend, wildfires in Indonesia, and presidential elections in Brazil pitting incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against challenger Flavio Bolsonaro.
items.title: FRANCE 24 Reviews Striking Images From a Week of Global Events

items.summary: A government survey finds Japan faces a shortage of Japanese language teachers before the April launch of its new foreign-worker program. Of 348 respondents, 125 organizations (35.9%) lack sufficient registered teachers with no prospects; only 51 (14.7%) have enough, while others are still working on it. Officials say they will make further efforts to secure instructors.
items.title: Japan Braces for Shortage of Language Teachers as New Worker Program Launches

items.summary: As Kenya records its second death from Ebola, with nine confirmed cases, the Red Cross has been training staff in Nairobi on handling victims. Dr Paul Olale said burials are a high-risk transmission route and teams need refreshers on safe practice. The ministry traced 135 contacts into quarantine; seven patients remain under care while no new cases appear outside Nairobi.
items.title: Red Cross Trains Staff as Kenya Records Second Ebola Death

items.summary: Under renewed Houthi attacks on its airport and oil facilities, Saudi Arabia has sought help from numerous allies, including the United States. Media report that President Trump declined a direct request for military action against the Houthis by Mohammed bin Salman, though the US is instead supplying intelligence and an AI-powered targeting tool through a new joint force command of roughly 100 to 200 soldiers. The system resembles the Maven Smart System, which analysts describe as aggregating vast streams of intelligence data to flag targets faster than human review alone could manage. Commentators caution that its effectiveness may be limited by Houthi mobility and terrain, while raising ethical concerns over civilian casualties from shortened strike timelines.
items.title: Saudi Arabia turns to US AI targeting amid Houthi escalation

items.summary: Elon Musk said his company SpaceX had restricted Ukraine's Starlink internet service, following Ukrainian officials' claim that connectivity problems appeared resolved. He accused Kyiv of violating terms by using the civilian service for military activity but denied responsibility for a separate issue with US-run Starshield. Serhii Beskrestnov called the post 'very strange', noting drones were speed-limited to 70-90km/h and could not operate on Russian territory, so deep strikes via commercial Starlink were physically impossible. Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara reported a stable connection with drone speeds exceeding 400km/h, up from the previous cut-out threshold of over 161km/h. Zelensky said 'The speeds are now where they need to be.' The comments followed remarks by Donald Trump telling Musk to restore the service amid tensions over strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.
items.title: Musk Says SpaceX Restricted Ukraine's Starlink After Service Restored

items.summary: That Girl Boina, a Kenyan food creator, took a two-week European holiday in 2025. A customer message revealed she had been asked to send money to an account other than the studio's, exposing employee theft at her Nairobi parlour, Waxaholic Studio. Revenue began falling in early 2025; although Boina considered closing earlier for lack of profit, she kept going until the discovery. She closed the business in October 2025 without finding a buyer. Her later TikTok video drew close to one million views and prompted other Kenyan owners to share similar theft experiences.
items.title: Kenyan food creator's business closed after staff theft exposed on holiday

items.summary: Public prosecutors in Okinawa Prefecture indicted U.S. Marine Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, on robbery and murder charges Sunday after a 39-year-old woman was found dead earlier that month. According to the indictment and other sources, Ballard allegedly strangled her with a telephone cord in a Naha hotel room between 2:10 a.m. and 4:15 a.m. on Oct. 3. Police arrested him around 11:30 a.m. that day.
items.title: U.S. Marine Indicted in Okinawa Robbery-Murder Case

items.summary: Australia's Kangaroos locked their Rugby League World Cup semifinal spot with a 36-22 win over Fiji at Lang Park. Despite trailing twice and entering as heavy outsiders, Tom Trbojevic's hat-trick sealed the berth after Fiji pushed hard through Semi Valemei.
items.title: Kangaroos beat Fiji in scare-ridden World Cup semifinal qualifier

items.summary: Demonstrators in Rome clashed with security forces Saturday after attempting to march toward the prime minister's office amid heightened Italian security following violent Milan protests last weekend. Police used water cannons and batons; one protester was seen injured, blood covering his head. Negotiations continued while some protesters threw bottles, explosive devices and fireworks. The unauthorized march ended peacefully near the Colosseum after demonstrators changed route. Authorities had detained 28 people as a preventive measure. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni thanked officers on X.
items.title: Rome Clashes as Protesters March Toward Prime Minister's Office

items.summary: The Bank of Israel said Saturday that cryptocurrencies cannot be used to circumvent potential economic sanctions, responding to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's proposal in a Friday interview to include them in contingency plans for possible banking and economic sanctions. Opposition leaders Yair Lapid and Yoav Horowitz warned the remarks could trigger capital flight and discourage investment ahead of Tuesday's Knesset elections.
items.title: Bank of Israel Rejects Crypto as Sanctions Loophole Amid Election Tensions

items.summary: In Wadeye, a remote Aboriginal community on Australia's Top End where only about one in five adults worked at the 2021 census and nearly everyone cites lack of jobs as its biggest problem, the Thamarrurr Sea Farmers have grown their mud crab operation into a commercial venture. Using Aboriginal coastal licences converted to full commercial status after a regional pause for stock recovery, they now hold up to 60 pots and employ nine workers, sending 35 to 50 kilograms of crabs to Darwin weekly. Tracey Leo of the Thamarrurr Development Corporation says a fully-fledged industry could emerge within a decade employing about 100 people, though she believes those outcomes will take time rather than rushing for numbers.
items.title: Wadeye Sea Farmers Grow Sustainable Mud Crab Industry Amid Job Crisis

items.summary: EL PAÍS reports from a Ukrainian command post in Kramatorsk that the front line shows hardly any change as Russia's full-scale invasion approaches its fifth anniversary. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy feels betrayed by U.S. President Donald Trump, accusing allies of doing too little after missile attacks and an alleged planned Starlink outage. Kyiv resumed strikes on Russian refineries despite a rejected energy ceasefire that never existed because Moscow opposed it. Soldiers say rain hampers drones but helps Russian infantry advance slowly through the besieged city.
items.title: Zelenskiy Feels Betrayed by Trump as Front Stalls in Rain Soaked Kramatorsk

items.summary: Actress and writer Zoe Kazan has become known chiefly as the creator, writer and executive producer of Netflix’s seven-episode adaptation of John Steinbeck’s 1952 novel East of Eden. Premiering October 1, the series places Florence Pugh’s Cathy Ames at its center rather than following her grandfather Elia Kazan’s 1955 film, which focused on James Dean’s Cal Trask. Strong early reviews have helped quiet critics who view it as commercially driven. Kazan shifted emphasis toward the novel’s female perspective and dialectics between philosophy and plot. She recently told GQ that there is a balancing act in the book between good and evil.
items.title: Zoe Kazan Reimagines Steinbeck’s East of Eden for Streaming

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India's Rs 169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at Info Valley-II in Jatni, near Bhubaneswar, Odisha. The institute will focus on training, research and capacity building.
items.title: Modi Inaugurates RBI Data Centre and Cybersecurity Institute in Odisha

items.summary: Tata Motors’ €3.91-billion tender offer for truckmaker Iveco reaches its final shareholder deadline of October 26, with settlement expected by October 30. Managing Director Girish Wagh is confident of clearing the reduced 80 per cent acceptance threshold, citing late-period tenders typical in such processes. Activist Petrus Advisers contests the valuation at roughly €18 per share, Italian Industry Minister Adolfo Urso demands industrial safeguards, and Indian brokerages remain divided on returns. The deal would create a commercial-vehicle group with about €21 billion annual revenue across India, Europe and the Americas, though weak European demand, debt and integration costs pose risks to profitability and Tata’s balance sheet.
items.title: Tata Motors Faces October Deadline on €3.91 Billion Iveco Bid

items.summary: A US intelligence memo dated October 23 warns that Iran has substantially increased efforts to target American diplomats and officials abroad, with lethal plots reaching advanced stages in the Middle East. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton conveyed it to Secretary of State Marco Rubio but declined to name targets or confirm an imminent attack. The warning accompanies a drawdown of US personnel at embassies across Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Lebanon, Qatar and Jordan amid fears that Iran-backed Houthis may widen attacks beyond Yemen.
items.title: US intel memo flags advanced Iranian plots, Houthi threat

items.summary: A 57-year-old retired senior Income Tax officer from Mumbai, a resident of Nagpur, became the victim of a cyber extortion network that impersonated police and RBI officials. Beginning on October 1, fraudsters posing as law enforcement claimed his identity was recovered at a Kashmir crime scene linked to terrorism and demanded he undergo surveillance while isolated in a hotel room. Over five days between October 2 and October 6, an individual claiming to be an IPS investigator conducted daily video interrogations. The scammers alleged his accounts were tied to money laundering under RBI authorization.
items.title: Retired Tax Officer Trapped in 'Digital Arrest' Scam

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India’s new Rs 169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, news agency Press Trust of India reported. The facilities, spread over 18.55 acres at Jatni, will host payment and settlement systems while supporting cybersecurity training. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra and Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi attended the event.
items.title: Modi inaugurates RBI's Rs 169-crore data centre and cybersecurity institute in Odisha

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India's ₹169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute on Sunday in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra, Odisha chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi and other officials were present, per news agency PTI. The 18.55-acre facility at Info Valley-II in Jatni had its foundation stone laid by then governor Shaktikanta Das on March 22, 2023. An official statement said it will host mission-critical payment systems and strengthen digital financial services. Around 2,100 security personnel were deployed for the visit. CM Majhi added that the centre's success would be judged by its long-term impact on digital infrastructure and data security.
items.title: Modi Inaugurates RBI Data Centre and Cybersecurity Institute in Odisha

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India’s new Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at Info Valley-II in Jatni, Khordha district. The 18.55-acre facility was built at an estimated cost of Rs 169 crore and is designed to strengthen cybersecurity training, digital infrastructure and critical payment systems such as RTGS and NEFT. Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman noted that UPI now processes more than 2,400 crore transactions a month.
items.title: Modi Inaugurates RBI’s ₹169-Crore Data Centre in Odisha

items.summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, speaking on the In Good Company podcast with Nicolai Tangen, called losing an early lead in social media his greatest mistake. He said there was a short moment when Google led everyone and he failed to act before Facebook overtook it. He took personal responsibility for being too slow.
items.title: Eric Schmidt names social media as his biggest failure as Google CEO

items.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge triggered a controversy on Sunday by calling Prime Minister Modi a habitual liar and saying Modi’s father would also be defeated, at an event in Patna. Union home minister Amit Shah accused Kharge of crossing limits, attributing the Congress's abuse to its electoral defeats since 2014 over 12 years.
items.title: Kharge's 'Modi ka baap' remark sparks BJP row

items.summary: Warren Buffett, who handed over the Berkshire Hathaway CEO role on January 1 and recently passed the Chairman title to his son Howard, offers six investment principles for retirees. He advises a 90% S&P 500 index fund and 10% short-term government bonds allocation in wills; paying off high-interest debt promptly; keeping cash as essential liquidity yet not an ideal asset; investing only within one's circle of competence; living below means, illustrated by his $31,500 Omaha home now worth about $1.3 million and a 2014 Cadillac XTS; and leaving children enough to do anything but nothing. The piece is written by Debaroti Adhikary, who notes the article does not constitute investment advice.
items.title: Buffett Shares Six Investment Rules After Stepping Down as CEO

items.summary: Indian equities fell further last week as midcap and smallcap shares declined sharply amid rising uncertainty, valuation concerns and tightening liquidity. Brent crude rose past $117 a barrel on Middle East tensions, while elevated US Treasury yields, foreign institutional investor selling and the Reliance Jio IPO weighed on sentiment. Hariselvan Radhakrishnan of HST Wealth said energy-price duration would shape spending pressure; Ravi Singh of Master Capital Services Ltd noted investors were reassessing speculative growth assets as Nifty declined 2.36% to near its 200-week EMA, with support at 22,300. Analysts will watch the October Federal Reserve meeting and earnings for stabilisation signals. The article was written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or Investment Adviser.
items.title: Five factors could decide Indian markets next week

items.summary: In an exclusive phone interview, Congress MP Imran Masood denied involvement in the student protest at Jamia Millia Islamia and blamed the university registrar and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh for divisive slogans. He said he opposed them on the spot while checking on agitating students' well-being. Separately, Union Home Minister Amit Shah condemned Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge for an abusive remark about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's family during a Patna speech.
items.title: Congress MP Denies RSS Role in Jamia Graffiti Row Amid Political Feud

items.summary: The Centre told the Supreme Court it is examining high margins and malpractices in medicine and hospital consumables, beyond its 30 per cent cap on anti-cancer drugs. Filed by Dr Sanjay Kulshrestha’s petition on October 12, the affidavit cites information asymmetries between patients and hospitals, doctors and pharmacies. It gave no timelines or extra drug categories. The 2019 cancer margin cap was set at 30 per cent of MRP, expected to lower MRPs by roughly 20 per cent to 70 per cent and save about Rs 2,500 crore a year.
items.title: Centre Examines High Margins Beyond Cancer Drugs

items.summary: The Hindu Association of Restaurants, Hotels, Aahar and Refreshments (HARHAR), supported by the World Hindu Economic Forum, held its HARHAR 2026 event in Juinagar West on Saturday evening. The gathering brought together Maharashtra ministers, elected representatives and hospitality stakeholders to discuss collective business growth, entrepreneurship and economic self-reliance. Officials urged members to translate unity into measurable outcomes.
items.title: HARHAR 2026 Unites Hindu-Owned Food Businesses for Economic Growth

items.summary: An accused man, Srinivasan T (45), arrested over narcotics worth around Rs 1.30 crore, escaped from a police lock-up in Dholpur district on Sunday after breaking a window between 3 am and 6 am while on remand at Deholi police station. Constables Vishnu and Jogesh were on duty when constable Manoj discovered him missing. Police launched a search across the district; he remains untraceable, with efforts underway to arrest him.
items.title: Drug Accused Escapes Police Custody in Rajasthan Lock-up Breakout

items.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of facilitating large-scale 'vote theft' favouring the BJP and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Addressing a function marking Bihar's first chief minister Sri Krishna Singh's 139th birth anniversary, he urged people to join an INDIA bloc protest in New Delhi on November 1 for the CEC's ouster. Kharge also attacked Nitish Kumar over RSS ties.
items.title: Kharge escalates vote-theft charge, demands CEC's removal in Patna

items.summary: IndiGo will shift 12 daily international departures from Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) to Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA), beginning in February 2027. The move, announced jointly with Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL), supports Terminal 1 redevelopment and redistributes air traffic across the dual-airport system. Air India Express will add four domestic flights at NMIA from December 2026, while IndiGo expands its international network to 12 destinations there.
items.title: IndiGo and Air India Express Shift Flights to Navi Mumbai Airport

items.summary: NFL safety Damar Hamlin helped 1,293 people learn hands-only CPR in one hour at Acrisure Stadium during the NFL Draft on 24 April 2026, setting a Guinness World Record for the most taught at a single location within an hour. The event was organised with the American Heart Association, the National Football League and Dr Mikhail Varshavski (Dr Mike), part of the association's Nation of Lifesavers campaign aiming to double survival rates by 2030. Hamlin, who survived cardiac arrest during a January 2023 game, said seeing people learn the life-saving skill in his hometown was deeply moving.
items.title: Damar Hamlin's CPR campaign sets a Guinness record in Pittsburgh

items.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge drew a political controversy after responding angrily to an audience member who shouted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi would not go. Interpreting the remark as defending Modi, Kharge said even Modi's father would have to go. The Bharatiya Janata Party condemned him for insulting the prime minister and his late father.
items.title: Kharge's Remark Sparks Political Controversy After Interrupter Clarifies Statement

items.summary: Four students at Jamia Millia Islamia in Delhi remained on hunger strike on Sunday (October 25) as a standoff over the restoration of their union continued. Around 200 students were inside the campus, with security personnel stationed outside and entry restricted through Gate No. 7. The agitation began October 12 after the university suspended its Students' Union in 2006 following violent clashes.
items.title: Jamia Students Continue Hunger Strike Over Union Restoration Standoff

items.summary: Rights groups and the Opposition condemned the arrests in Odisha of doctor Randall Sequeira and Dalit activist Laxman Naik, alleging a crackdown on Adivasi and Dalit communities opposing mining projects. Jan Swasthya Abhiyan demanded their release and called charges fabricated; CPI(M) Odisha blamed Vedanta and Adani-linked repression; Congress leaders Jairam Ramesh and Mahua Moitra questioned due process. The arrests relate to an April clash in Rayagada over a road linked to the Sijimali bauxite mine, where more than 50 persons were injured.
items.title: Rights Groups and Opposition Condemn Arrests of Two Odisha Activists

items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar warned private companies, especially Bengaluru's IT sector, not to deliberately exclude Kannadigas from jobs. Speaking on X, he said the government would take action if any firm sidelined local candidates and reaffirmed that Karnataka treats its Kannadiga talent with pride. The remarks followed a viral video of a young woman alleging language-based hiring discrimination.
items.title: Karnataka CM warns IT firms against sidelining Kannadigas

items.summary: Nadia Hashimi is an Afghan-American paediatrician and novelist whose latest book, City of Widows, centres women in the years after the Taliban regained power in Afghanistan. She spoke to Scroll about how her novel moves away from Western media portrayals that reduce Afghan women to victims or symbols. The idea for the story came while she worked on psychosocial support for people evacuated from Kabul airport in August 2021, when she encountered accounts of women who served in the Female Tactical Platoon and showed up with their hair and makeup done; one replied: “If I die tonight, I die pretty.” Hashimi wanted readers to see Afghan women rise to their full height rather than be lionised. She argues that storytelling is a form of resistance against regimes controlling what women can say or become, noting the Taliban banned books by university women and restricted girls’ education beyond sixth grade.
items.title: Afghan Novelist Frames Women as Full Human Beings, Not Symbols

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department said the Depression over the East Central and Southeast Bay of Bengal will intensify into a Deep Depression, then a cyclonic storm by Tuesday morning. It is expected to reach near the Andhra Pradesh coast around October 28 and make landfall between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm with winds of 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph. Odisha and Andhra Pradesh governments have reviewed response plans amid forecasts of heavy rainfall.
items.title: IMD Warns Cyclone Arnab Will Intensify Into Severe Storm

items.summary: In a holiday-shortened week, the BSE Sensex fell 1,605.44 points (2.15%) and the NSE Nifty dropped 546.15 points (2.36%). Total market capitalisation of BSE-listed firms slid Rs 20,78,774.28 crore to Rs 4,51,83,393.14 crore from the October 16 level. Of the top-10 companies, eight lost value totalling Rs 1,55,671.9 crore; HDFC Bank and Reliance Industries were among the biggest losers, while Tata Consultancy Services and Larsen & Toubro gained.
items.title: Eight of India's Top-10 Firms See Market Cap Erode

items.summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors significantly reduced selling last week and turned net buyers on two trading days, easing pressure after Rs 35,861 crore of net withdrawals in September. Cumulative FPI outflows from Indian equities reached Rs 3.08 lakh crore in 2026 versus Rs 1.66 lakh crore in all of 2025.
items.title: FPI Selling Moderates as Investors Turn Net Buyers in October

items.summary: An author argues that assessments of Narendra Modi's record focus too much on welfare schemes and not enough on the scale of his infrastructure effort. The piece notes capital expenditure grew more than fivefold to over ₹12 lakh crore since 2014, with spending directed at transport, industrial land, electronics, defence, space, startups and finance. It cites examples such as Dedicated Freight Corridors, ready-made industrial towns like Dholera and Tumakuru, the Phased Manufacturing Programme that made India a major mobile-phone maker, chip plants backed by the ₹76,000 crore India Semiconductor Mission, rising defence exports to about 80 countries, private-sector space launches from Skyroot's Vikram-1 in July 2026 and GIFT City. The author conveys some gaps, including that only 15 to 20 per cent of a smartphone made in India is added locally and research spending needs to rise above 1 per cent of GDP, then frames the wider infrastructure as Modi's main legacy while noting much work remains unfinished.
items.title: Modi's Wider Infrastructure Legacy Is Under-Appreciated, Author Says
